newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak govt replaces Deputy Fin Minister Magula.
newsitem.headline: Slovak govt replaces Deputy Fin Minister Magula.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday replaced Deputy Finance Minister Jozef Magula after he openly criticised recent amendments to the country's securities legislation.

The law, which had been sent back to parliament by President Michal Kovac for revision, omitted a controversial clause which would have allowed major shareholders to arbitrarily cancel trade in an issue.

But Magula, widely known for his battles against the country's largest investment funds and investment companies, said he was disappointed with both the draft and the final version of the legislation, which was approved in December.
"I offered my resignation at the end of last year, mainly due to my opposition to some of the latest changes on the capital market," Magula told Reuters.
The government said in a statement that it had replaced Magula with Peter Stanek, an economic adviser to Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.

The approved version of the law forces trading of registered shares onto accredited bourses. It also forbids the change of registered shares into bearer shares, which was permitted under the previous law.
"I think the compromise final version included only weak corrections of the proposal, which I had seen as completely unsatisfactory," he said.
Magula however rejected speculation that there was a rift between him and the government, adding that "it (his removal) was the result of an agreement and that...nothing special had happened".
He declined to comment on a report by the Slovak official news agency TASR that he "would (probably) take a high function in the National Bank of Slovakia", the country's central bank.
"I think that (TASR) did not make it up...but I cannot tell you anything further," he said. Central bank officials would not comment on the news.
